title: Ziyarid dynasty
capsule: In the mid-tenth century the Ziyarids — an Iranian dynasty of Gilaki origin founded by Mardavij ibn Ziyar — held Tabaristan and Gurgan on the southern Caspian shore from their seats at Gurgan and Astarabad. After Mardavij's assassination in 935 his brother Vushmgir (r. 935–967) led the dynasty, but he ruled as a contested vassal, his lands repeatedly seized and recovered in the three-way struggle among the Buyids of western Iran and the Samanids of Khurasan, to whom he turned for support. His sons Bisutun and then Qabus ibn Vushmgir succeeded him, until Qabus was driven from Tabaristan around 980 by the Buyid Adud al-Dawla, beginning a long Ziyarid exile.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory in Tabaristan and Jurjan is well-established; the fluctuating extent of Ziyarid control under Buyid and Ghaznavid pressure is incompletely mapped.
